summary: T. S. Devadoss was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who held posts at the University of Madras, where he was attested in 1994 and attested as Professor in 2008.

T. S. Rukmani specializes in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held positions at Miranda House, University of Delhi (attested 1983–1989) and Concordia University as Chairperson of Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion (attested 1989).

T. S. Srinivasa Sastri worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972, 2007), serving as Professor (attested 1984–1992), and taught scholars including Yoshitsugu Sawai, Robert P. Goldman, and Ludo Rocher.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry studied at the University of Mysore under teachers including D. L. Narasimhachar and Harogadde Manappa Nayak. Specializing in linguistics and Indology, he taught at Osmania University, Kannada University, and Mysore, where he was Professor (1984–1994).
T. Venkatacharya was an Indologist and linguist who taught at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1971) and as Professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979).

T. W. Rhys Davids earned a Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. He founded the Pali Text Society, serving as its first president (~1881–1922), and held professorships at the University of London and the University of Manchester.
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa studied at Kyoto University and worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He taught at Tokai University, Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and Ryukoku University, and served as President of Toho Gakkai (~2007–2011).

Tadashi Inoue studied at the University of Tokyo. Specializing in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology, he held posts at the Kyoto National Museum, Iida City Museum (Director 1988–2006), Nara University, Bukkyo University, and Kyoto University of the Arts.
Tadashi Sekino was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and later served there as Professor Emeritus (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani completed doctoral studies at Waseda University, studied at Kyoto University, and studied under Yuichi Kajiyama. Focusing on Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he was Professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (attested 1996–2000).
Tadashi Toda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski earned a Ph.D. from the University of London. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he held positions at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Tring, and SOAS University of London.
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Ming-Wood Liu.

Taido Kitamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held academic posts at Shuchiin University, including assistant professor (attested 1980) and further appointments attested from 1994 to 1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton studied at Columbia University and the Graduate Theological Union. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, he has taught at Loyola University Chicago, the Institute of Buddhist Studies, Otani University, and the University of San Francisco.

Taijun Inokuchi worked in Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1963–1987) and served as representative of The Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue. A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held academic positions at Komazawa, Japan Women's University, and the University of Tokyo.
Taiken Kyuma completed a PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, he served as Associate Professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
